cards.explanation: The answer is the courtyard of the guard. Verse 2 says Jeremiah was imprisoned in the courtyard of the guard, which was in the palace of the king of Judah. Locked up, and the address still has the word PALACE in it. Five stars for the location, zero stars for the stay.

The answer is capture, friends. Zedekiah asks, “Why are you prophesying like this?” and then repeats what Jeremiah says the LORD said: “…and he will capture it.” (Jeremiah 32:3). The king is quoting the message right back at him. Jeremiah is already imprisoned in the courtyard of the guard when Zedekiah says it (Jeremiah 32:2).

The answer is False, friends. Verse 5 says that if you fight against the Chaldeans, you will not succeed. The message says the fighting won't work. It's a hard word, and I think it's not the one Zedekiah was hoping to hear.

The answer is Anathoth, friends. The LORD tells Jeremiah that Hanamel will say, “Buy for yourself my field in Anathoth…” (Jeremiah 32:7). The LORD even tells him the cousin is coming before the cousin knocks. That's better notice than I get when somebody says they're stopping by.

The answer is True, friends. Jeremiah is the one telling it, and he says, “Then, as the LORD had said, my cousin Hanamel came to me in the courtyard of the guard…” (Jeremiah 32:8). The LORD said he would come, and he came, right to the locked-up prophet. Jeremiah says that's when he knew this was the word of the LORD.

The answer is that this was the word of the LORD, friends. Jeremiah says, “Then I knew that this was the word of the LORD.” (Jeremiah 32:8). The LORD had told him Hanamel was coming, and then Hanamel showed up with the request. When it lines up like that, you don't need a second opinion.

The answer is False, friends. Jeremiah called in witnesses in verse 10, and verse 12 says the witnesses were signing the purchase agreement. It also says all the Jews sitting in the courtyard of the guard were there when he gave the deed to Baruch. That's the opposite of quiet.

The answer is Baruch son of Neriah, friends. Verse 12 says Jeremiah gave the deed to Baruch son of Neriah, the son of Mahseiah, in the sight of Hanamel, the witnesses and all the Jews sitting in the courtyard of the guard. Notice how many names the writer included. I can barely fit my own name on a cookie box.

The answer is to preserve them for a long time, friends. Verse 14 says to put both deeds in a clay jar “…to preserve them for a long time.” The sealed copy and the open copy go in together. Just a jar and a plan that lasts.

The answer is again, friends. The LORD of Hosts says, “Houses, fields, and vineyards will again be bought in this land.” (Jeremiah 32:15). Right now there's a siege, and the word is that buying and selling will come back. That's why the jar matters.
